text.content: Meridian Consulting's agent has been built, refined, secured, end-to-end tested, and audited. The platform decision has been documented and defended on paper. The final step before deployment approval is the stakeholder presentation.

text.content: Meridian's CIO has allocated thirty minutes for the review. The first ten minutes are a live demonstration of the agent's capabilities. The remaining twenty are a formal architectural defense. The CIO wants to understand not just that the agent works, but why it was built the way it was and whether that architecture can be trusted handling confidential client operational data.

A defense that cannot explain the platform choice against specific enterprise constraints does not earn approval. Both must be precise, honest, and grounded in the agent's actual architecture.

text.content: "This looks capable. But I need to understand the governance picture before I approve production deployment. text.content: Argument 1 - Why self-hosted Flowise is the correct production path

rich_text.plain_text: Argument 1 - Why self-hosted Flowise is the correct production path

text.content: Explain what the current self-hosted Docker prototype provides and what it does not yet provide for production. Reference the four infrastructure dimensions (hosting, observability, security at scale, and governance). Explain why the migration from the current Docker prototype to a production-grade Flowise deployment is a well-defined path rather than a rebuild where the canvas logic, system prompt, Document Store configuration, and routing architecture all carry forward. Only the infrastructure layer changes.

text.content: Argument 2 - Why the current Gemini API setup needs a production upgrade

rich_text.plain_text: Argument 2 - Why the current Gemini API setup needs a production upgrade

text.content: The current build uses the Gemini API free tier via Google AI Studio credentials. Explain the data handling implications of the free tier for a consulting firm processing confidential client operational data. Reference the specific concern: on the free tier, data sent to the API may be used by Google to improve its models. Explain what the upgrade path is (moving to a paid Gemini API tier or Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform) and what that provides in terms of data privacy, SLAs, and GDPR compliance.

text.content: Argument 3 - Why Microsoft Copilot Studio is the wrong choice for Meridian

rich_text.plain_text: Argument 3 - Why Microsoft Copilot Studio is the wrong choice for Meridian

text.content: Address the CIO's colleague's suggestion directly. Your argument must cover three points specifically:

rich_text.plain_text: Address the CIO's colleague's suggestion directly. Your argument must cover three points specifically:

text.content: Copilot Studio's governance advantages are predicated on an existing Microsoft 365 ecosystem (Azure AD, SharePoint, Teams) that Meridian does not use. The inherited governance controls provide no value to an organisation without that infrastructure.

rich_text.plain_text: Copilot Studio's governance advantages are predicated on an existing Microsoft 365 ecosystem (Azure AD, SharePoint, Teams) that Meridian does not use. The inherited governance controls provide no value to an organisation without that infrastructure.

text.content: Copilot Studio's connector ecosystem is optimised for Microsoft tools. Integrating with Meridian's custom internal APIs and the Gemini model already validated in the build requires custom connector development that negates the low-code governance benefit.

rich_text.plain_text: Copilot Studio's connector ecosystem is optimised for Microsoft tools. Integrating with Meridian's custom internal APIs and the Gemini model already validated in the build requires custom connector development that negates the low-code governance benefit.

text.content: Rebuilding in Copilot Studio means abandoning three sprints of validated canvas logic such as the Document Store configuration, the Condition Agent Node routing, the retry logic, and the Human Input approval checkpoint and then rebuilding it from scratch in an unfamiliar platform immediately before deployment. The risk profile of that decision is not justified by the governance benefit, which does not materialise without a Microsoft ecosystem.

text.content: Takeaway:

rich_text.plain_text: Takeaway:

text.content: The demo script demonstrates that the agent works under realistic conditions including failure conditions. The platform defense demonstrates that the architectural decisions behind it were deliberate, evidence-based, and defensible against enterprise constraints. Together they represent the two capabilities that matter most when an AI agent moves from a project to a product: the ability to show it working and the ability to explain why it was built the way it was.
